summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The five calls stay neutral with low conviction: Apple slipped below its trend line, Microsoft climbed back above it, and Amgen and Gilead are still stretched. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: This week two runners swapped places: Apple slowed down and Microsoft picked up again. That kind of back and forth is why guessing runners did no better than luck before. The brain only watches with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. If this week's buy of the whole-market fund is not done yet, do it now; otherwise nothing to do until next week's buy. Money we may need soon stays safe. The market's trend still leans down, which is ordinary.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The weekly bet game stands at two weeks won and one lost, and this week's bet is behind so far. That swing from week to week is exactly what luck looks like.

Third, a lesson. Apple and Microsoft swapped places on our trend check within two days. A rule that flips that easily cannot be trusted with money, and it is a good picture of why owning the whole market spares us from choosing.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
